findings_fixed: H1 (high, correctness/AC): a rejected save rendered NOTHING to the admin. ValidationException was attached to data.definition, whose only component is Filament\Forms\Components\Hidden - a bare <input> with no error slot and columnSpan hidden - and throwing ValidationException by hand from save() bypasses Filament's own onValidationError toast. The page blade has zero error surfaces. VERIFIED independently against vendor source. Fixed by also sending a persistent danger Notification.

M2 (medium, correctness/AC): partial zip resolution was still silent. ST_Union over ARRAY[...] drops NULL members, so polygons + an unresolvable zip produced a non-empty geometry, passed the emptiness guard, and silently discarded the zip. Fixed by checking unresolved zips independently of emptiness. Proven red->green by a new test.

M3 (medium, test integrity): both new Materializer tests could pass for the wrong reason. (a) expectException(RuntimeException) also accepts QueryException (which extends RuntimeException), so the test would pass if the UPDATE failed before the guard ran - now asserts the message. (b) $this->fail() throws AssertionFailedError, which also extends RuntimeException, so it was being swallowed by the adjacent catch - restructured to assert on the caught message outside the try.

L1 (low, correctness): the zip-lookup helper could itself throw a QueryException (a RuntimeException) while the sentinel was still null, masking the real cause with an unhandled 500. Now degrades to an empty list via catch (Throwable).
L2 (low, test adequacy): restored the definition-normalization coverage lost with the replaced test, via the rejection message (duplicates collapsed, integer zip cast to string).

RN2-M1 (medium, correctness): the NULL-drop insight was applied to ManageZones but NOT to Materializer, which uses the identical ST_Union(ARRAY[...]) construct. A run area of [valid polygon, state 'ZZ'] produced a non-empty geometry, passed the emptiness guard, and was stamped materialized while silently excluding the entire state - which then under-clips every Scout heatmap with no signal. Added unresolvedReferences() checking state/msa references against tiger_data.state_all/tl_2019_us_county (whereNotNull on the geometry column). Proven red->green: the new test does not throw at all against RN=2 code.

RN2-L1 (low, correctness - REGRESSION introduced by the RN=2 fix): unresolvedZipCodes() swallowed Throwable INSIDE the save transaction. Postgres aborts a transaction on any statement error, so the swallowed error made the subsequent COMMIT come back as a silent ROLLBACK while save() fell through to Analytics::track and the 'Zone saved' success toast - precisely AC-2 inverted, reintroduced by the hardening meant to protect it. Hoisted the lookup ABOVE the transaction (it reads nothing the transaction writes), which also takes the reference-table scan out from under the zones row lock.

RN2-L2 (low, correctness): unresolvedZipCodes() tested row existence, but zcta5_all.the_geom is nullable and a NULL geometry contributes nothing to the union - so such a zip was reported resolved and silently dropped. Now whereNotNull('the_geom'). Same fix applied to the new Materializer reference check.

RN2 non-scoring: corrected the H1 comment's rationale (BasePage::$reportValidationErrorUsing is never assigned in this app, so there is no Filament toast to bypass - the real reason is that `definition` has nowhere to render); softened the over-claimed strval assertion in the normalization test's docblock.

RN3-M1 (medium, incomplete fix): unresolvedReferences() only inspected state/msa entries with a non-empty string reference, so a RECOGNIZED kind that yields no SQL piece slipped through - notably `geometry` supplied as a JSON string (pieceFor returns null because is_array fails), an integer state FIPS, or an empty msa reference. inputs=[polygon-as-JSON-string, state TX] therefore stamped materialized covering Texas only, silently dropping the operator's polygon: the same silent-drop the round-3 guard exists to prevent, through a different door. inputs is Backyard-owned and unvalidated in Clarity, and the SIBLING builder (Zone::rebuildGeometryFromDefinition) explicitly tolerates a JSON-string polygon, so the shape is plausible. Now tracked per-entry and folded into the same rejection. Proven by a new test.

RN3-L1 (low): the try in unresolvedReferences() wrapped the WHOLE two-kind loop, so a failure on the msa pass discarded an already-collected state finding and returned []. Moved inside the loop - degrade for that kind only, never discard findings already collected.

RN3-L2 (low, test adequacy): the danger Notification - the only USER-VISIBLE half of the H1 fix - was unpinned by any test; deleting those lines left the suite green while the originally reported symptom returned. Now asserted with ->assertNotified('Zone not saved'), an API this repo already uses in ZoneResourceTest.

RN4-M1 (medium, incomplete fix): $malformed was collected in the pieceFor loop but the `$pieces === []` early return fired BEFORE it was ever read, so an ALL-malformed input set still no-oped silently. That is the likelier production shape - one bad serialization drops every entry, not just one - and on a re-materialize it left the row holding its OLD geometry and OLD materialized_at while the operator's boundary change was ignored with no signal. Moved the rejection ahead of the no-pieces return. The two documented-contract cases are untouched and still return early silently: empty inputs, and unrecognized-kind-only (kind 'nonsense' produces no $malformed entry). Proven red->green.
findings_residual: RN2-M2 (medium, PRE-EXISTING, not introduced here): the `definition` ->rule() path (empty polygons AND empty zips) also renders nothing, for the same reason H1 did - the Hidden component has no error slot and the page has no form-level error region. Deliberately NOT fixed: it is a pre-existing validation-display bug on a different trigger than this ticket's zip path, and fixing it properly means a blade/view change outside target_files. This ticket already widened scope once by explicit operator decision (Q5); widening again unasked is not the driver's call. RECOMMEND a follow-up ticket - it is cheap and it is the same 'doesn't register' symptom class users report.

L3 (low, conditional): the Materializer throw escapes the queued MaterializeOrgRunArea. Under QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync it 500s Backyard's signed webhook; production runs Horizon {low} with tries=1, so it is one failed_jobs row - the intended loud signal. Not fixed: would touch BackyardController, outside target_files. Both review rounds independently agreed this triage is correct.

PRE-EXISTING, surfaced by the sweep, NOT introduced here: Materializer::polygonPiece() feeds arbitrary Backyard-authored GeoJSON into ST_GeomFromGeoJSON with no ring-arity check, where the Zone side has geoJsonHasValidRing() for exactly that reason.

Non-scoring: Tailwind 4 auto-source-detection minted/dropped phantom utilities in the built theme CSS because it scans non-source text (gained .invisible, lost .justify-end). Verified harmless - zero justify-end usages in app/ or resources/views. Worth an `@source not` for docs/, .ai/, tests/ in a follow-up.

Test-adequacy gap (non-scoring): the H1 danger Notification is not pinned by an assertNotified() assertion. Its delivery chain was verified by reading Filament vendor source, and Phase 6 browser QA confirms it visually, but a future deletion of those lines would not fail the suite.

RN5-M1 (medium, PRE-EXISTING, not introduced here): hydrateZips() silently truncates definition.zip_codes during edit hydration - it drops a zip with no signal on three paths, then syncEditingState $wire.set's the TRUNCATED list back as the authoritative definition, so the in-code comment 'the saved record is still authoritative server-side' is false by design. A transient zip-search failure permanently deletes that zip on the next save under a green 'Zone saved', and for an unresolvable zip the new server guard is unreachable from the browser because the client strips it first. NOT fixed here: pre-existing, and its sibling half (geometryToRings dropping interior rings) is explicitly owned by the unmerged DEV-2557 per prep-context Q4, so a fix would collide with that branch. STRONGLY RECOMMEND a follow-up ticket - this is the same defect class as D1/D4.

RN5-M2 (medium, test adequacy): no test resolves a REAL state/msa reference, so unresolvedReferences() is only ever proven to fire, never proven to stay quiet on a good reference - while whereNotNull('simplified_geom') is the highest-risk line in the diff. Not closable in this harness (same spatial_ref_sys wall as the zip happy path). Routed to QA as a verify step plus the production premise below, rather than a sixth review round.

RN5 non-scoring, self-inflicted: the `...$malformed` spread at Materializer.php:78 is dead after the new pre-transaction throw. Harmless clutter; fixing it would invalidate reviewed_sha and force a sixth round for a no-op.

ac.item: AC-1 — Zip-code zone creation reliably works across zip codes that HAVE a Census ZCTA boundary.
ac.evidence: Browser: 75201 resolved, drew a polygon, saved, and the geometry re-rendered on a fresh re-open (A4, A5). This is the path the PHP harness cannot reach at all.

ac.item: AC-2 — A zip that cannot be resolved to a boundary fails LOUDLY, never silently 'saves' an invisible zone.
ac.evidence: A zip with no usable boundary is refused with a visible red persistent 'Zone not saved' toast naming it (A6); a valid zip alongside it does not mask the failure (A8); and the null/empty-geom zone count is still 0 afterwards, independently re-verified (A7).

ac.item: AC-3 — Malformed or truncated zip input never silently attaches an unrelated zip's boundary.
ac.evidence: A 4-digit fragment is rejected as malformed rather than prefix-matched (A2); a 5-digit zip with no row reports no boundary rather than attaching rows[0] (A3); a mixed batch keeps the good token and names both bad ones (A10).

ac.item: AC-4 — Confirm whether this is a data/formatting validation issue or a lookup/geocoding failure.
ac.evidence: Not a verifiable behaviour — it is the ticket's own question. The answer is BOTH: D1/D2 were server-side validation/guard defects and D3/D4 were client-side lookup defects. It stays N/A rather than SATISFIED because Q1 was never answered: the reporter never said which zip codes failed, so this ticket cannot claim which defect produced the reported symptom.

ac.item: AC-5 — A zip with no Census boundary shows a clear, actionable error and the admin can draw the zone manually.
ac.evidence: The error is specific and actionable ('No Census boundary found for ZIP code(s): 75203. Remove them, or draw the zone manually.'), and the admin can act on it in place: after a rejection, removing the zip and drawing the polygon by hand saved successfully without a reload (A9).

ac.item: AC-6 — OrgRunArea materialization cannot silently persist a NULL/empty geometry.
ac.evidence: Materializer throws rather than stamping a NULL/empty geometry for an unresolvable state (B4) or msa reference, and — the case with no prior coverage — stays quiet and produces a valid ST_MultiPolygon on a good polygon-only run area (B3). Caveat: both reference tables are empty in this environment, so the state/msa HAPPY path is unverified here.
